subject: Anchoring credits vs. on-call retainer — proposed tradeoffs for OrbitHealth
participants_external: anna.keller@orbithealth.com (Anna Keller, Head of Cloud Ops)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Anna Keller <anna.keller@orbithealth.com>, procurement@orbithealth.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Anchoring credits — quick framing and ask

Anna / OrbitHealth procurement team,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I wanted to put a short framing note on the table so we can move pricing and packaging toward legal:

- Ask from the customer side: reduce the upfront platform fee by replacing a portion of the fee with a quarterly on-call retainer credit and a smaller amortized platform fee over 12 months (anchor the commitment to a 12-month minimum).
- Our trade: we can offer a 20% reduction to the platform fee if OrbitHealth accepts a 12-month anchored commit and a 200-hour annual on-call retainer, payable as a separate line item. We can also amortize the platform fee across the term for accounting clarity.

Can you confirm the target ARR and which teams would own the on-call budget? Once I have that I can run the concession through commercial/finance to check approvals. Attaching the SOC2 summary you asked for and the initial pricing workbook we used in the demo.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm the on-call owner and a rough expected monthly run-rate.
2) We (Redwood) return with two concrete term-sheet options: (A) higher upfront / lower on-call retainer; (B) lower upfront / on-call-credit swap (what we sketched above).

Thanks — I’ll loop Marissa into the follow-ups for the term-sheet.

—Jonas

Jonas — thanks, this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- OrbitHealth target ARR for inference is approx $1.2M year one if usage stays within projections.
- On-call budget lives with Cloud Ops (that’s me) and will need a separate PO unless bundled into platform fee as a capitalized cost.
- We’re interested in option B (lower upfront / on-call-credit swap) but need the net present cost to be within the same payback period our finance team already models (9 months).

Two asks before we take to procurement: 
1) Can Redwood provide a worked example showing net effective price over 12 months (with both the 12-month amortization and the on-call retainer swap)?
2) Can you list the SLOs tied to the on-call retainer (hours, response-time tiers) — we need that to justify the retainer in our internal chargebacks.

If you can get that over today we’ll aim to have procurement review by EOD Wednesday.

Thanks — attaching a short internal note on PO flows so you can see how the chargeback will be processed.

Jonas — ran the numbers and sketched two simple term scenarios (summary below). Full workbook attached.

Summary (assumptions: $1.2M ARR baseline usage, baseline platform fee $180k upfront):

Option A — Standard upfront
- Platform fee: $180k upfront (not amortized)
- On-call retainer: optional, billed separately at $55k/year for 200 hours
- Effective annual cost: $1.435M (includes platform + usage)

Option B — Anchor + on-call-credit swap (customer-preferred)
- Platform fee: $144k (20% concession) amortized monthly over 12 months = $12k/mo
- On-call retainer: 200-hours credited against invoice; gross retainer value $55k but customer pays $25k in cash and the rest is credited over the term -> net cash outlay lower up-front
- Effective annual cost: ~ $1.32M (depends on how credit is applied to monthly invoices) — net present modeled to hit ~9-month payback for OrbitHealth when credits applied monthly.

SLO language (draft):
- Priority 1 (system outage impacting production inference): 1 hour response, 4 hour mitigation commitment, escalation to named SRE lead if unresolved after 2 hours.
- Priority 2 (degradation): 4 hour response, 24 hour remediation plan.
- On-call hours apply during business hours by default; 24/7 coverage available as an upgrade line item.

I attached: proposed_term_sheet_v2.docx and the workbook (redwood_proposal_v1.xlsx with the new tabs). Naomi — please confirm whether finance is comfortable capitalizing platform fee and the feasibility of amortizing internally for accounting.

—Ben Carter

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Anchoring credits — finance note and recommended wording

Team — quick finance/legal guidance:

- Capitalization: Redwood can present the platform fee as an invoiced upfront service. Whether OrbitHealth capitalizes will be their accounting policy. For our proposal, offering amortization as a customer-facing payment schedule (12 monthly invoices) is fine; finance is okay with that structure provided invoices are clear and collectable.
- Net impact: the Option B mix Ben modeled looks acceptable from our side as long as we: (1) keep the amortization schedule in the contract, (2) limit the refundable portion of any credits to actual on-call consumption (i.e., unused hours do not auto-refund but can be carried one quarter), and (3) require a minimum notice for cancellation (60 days) to avoid churn risk.

Recommended contract language snippet (short):
"Platform Fee and On-call Credit: Customer agrees to a 12-month anchored commitment. Redwood will invoice the platform fee over 12 monthly installments. Customer purchases a 200-hour on-call retainer valued at $55,000; $25,000 will be invoiced as cash at contract start and the remaining $30,000 will be provided as invoice credit to be applied monthly subject to on-call consumption. Unused credit may be carried forward for one calendar quarter and is non-refundable. Cancellation requires 60 days written notice and pro-rated final invoice applies."

If everyone agrees to that language I’ll prepare a short redline for legal and we can route to OrbitHealth procurement.

—Naomi Feldman
Head of Revenue Finance | Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com

Anna / OrbitHealth team —

Thanks for the quick turn. Ben and Naomi sent back a worked example and recommended contract snippet (below). High level proposal (what we want you to review):

1) 12-month anchored commitment
2) Platform fee: $144k (20% concession) invoiced monthly over 12 months ($12k/mo)
3) On-call retainer: 200 hours, gross value $55k — customer pays $25k upfront, $30k issued as monthly credits applied to invoices; unused credits can carry for one quarter, no refunds.
4) SLOs: P1 — 1 hour response, P2 — 4 hour response; escalation to named SRE after 2 hours for P1. 24/7 coverage optional extra.

Action items:
- If OrbitHealth is comfortable with the language Naomi suggested, reply with confirmation and we’ll route a short term-sheet + redline to procurement/legal.
- Also confirm who signs the PO (procurement@orbithealth.com or your finance lead) so we can include the right signature block.

We’ll attach the term-sheet and the workbook to the DocuSign packet once you confirm.

Best,
Jonas
